Ezek. 8.18. Zech. 7.13.</ns0:note> they <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The cruel oppressours, these Tyrannical Judges that pityed none, devoured all, and feared not the Divine vengeance.</ns0:note> cry unto the LORD <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">As if they were his, and as if he were bound to deliver; they then shall own he can, and none else can deliver them, and they will expect a saving hand after all their Rebellions against, and contempts of God.</ns0:note>, but he will not hear them <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">As they heard the cry of the op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pressed, but would not hear; so God will hear the cry of their distresses, but not hear the requests they make; he will do no more for them, then as if he did not hear them, he will be as a stranger to their case.</ns0:note>: he will even hide his face from them <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">They turned away their face from beholding and pitying the poor, now God will turn away his eye from them, and as if unconcern'd, leave them to their own distresses, and their Enemies rage and cruelty.</ns0:note> at that time <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">This added to assure them they should have least respect from God, when they need it most, so they shall receive what they gave, judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment without mercy, as 'tis <ns0:hi>Iam.</ns0:hi> 2.13.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">This speaks both the reason why, and the manner how God will thus leave them to the oppressour, the greatness of their sin deserved this, and such was the quality of their sins, that nothing fit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter than a retaliation to punish the sin, convince the sinner, teach the world righteousness, and to vindicate God.</ns0:note>, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings <ns0:hi>z.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 ¶ Thus saith the LORD <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Now <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> in the Name of the Lord foretels what shall become of false Prophets, he had frankly dealt with the secu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lars, now he deals as plainly with the Ecclesiasticks.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 56.10, 11. Ezek. 22.25.</ns0:note> concerning the prophets that make my people err <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Tho' he give them the Title they assume to themselves, yet he doth very fully describe them, and shews they are false Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, they err, and make others to err with them. <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> is too apt to mistake his God, and his wayes, these false Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets make them err more, both concerning their former wayes of Religion, and civil policie, and concerning their present danger and duty; and concerning future judgments and pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nishments.</ns0:note>, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 2.11.</ns0:note> bite with their teeth <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">When they are furnisht with gifts, and well fed.</ns0:note>, and cry, Peace <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">They promise great prosperity, they pretend to give assu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rance from God, that all shall go well with <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and none of the dismal woes threatned by <ns0:hi>Micah,</ns0:hi> and such like Prophets should ever be verifyed on them.</ns0:note>: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 13.18, 19.</ns0:note> he that putteth not into their mouthes <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">But those who will not feed these false Prophets, that bid them not welcom to their Tables, nor make good chear for them.</ns0:note>, they even prepare war against him <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">They do threaten with war, and all calamities that attend it, or else as Enemies prepared, they work them all the mischief they can, and shew what God they serve, even the God of this world, and their own bellies.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

I rather take this night to be a night of distresses, a time of great Calamities up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on these Prophets more than ordinary, and upon all the peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple they seduced.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> unto you <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Deceivers, and false Prophets.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>from a vision.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> that ye shall not have a vision <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">You shall no more pretend to have a vision, you shall not dare any more to foretel any thing to this people.</ns0:note>, and it shall be dark <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Very calamitous time to all, but most to you who lived upon lying Visions, and now shall starve for want of them.</ns0:note> unto you, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>from di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vining.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> that ye shall not divine <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Have neither skill, nor will any more to set up for your selves in that Trade, being found great Impostors, and such as have seduced this people into sin first, and misery next, they will be inraged against you, and you shall not safely appear among them.</ns0:note>, and the sun shall go down over the prophets <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">A proverbial speech, and contains much the same, that night and dark do contain. Perhaps this intimates the visible hand of God ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />traordinarily against them, and making their sorrows the more dreadful, as darkness by the Sun going down at Noon, would speak it self an extraordinary judgment, and most terrifie the world.</ns0:note>, and the day shall be dark <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The best circumstances any of them shall be in, shall be so sad and woful, that they shall not know which way to take for themselves, or direct for others.</ns0:note> over them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:181" />7 Then <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">In the dayes of this Calamity, which shall confute all the flattering promises of these Prophets.</ns0:note> shall the seers <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Who call'd them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves, were accounted by others, and were advised with as men that had Visions from God, were Prophets in name and repute with the deceived people.</ns0:note> be ashamed <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Their Impostures being detected they shall be covered with shame, the people shall talk what they are, and tell them to their faces where ever they meet them that they are false and lying Varlets, not worthy to live, and the very Consciences of these men shall then fly in their faces and upbraid them.</ns0:note>, and the diviners confounded <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Diviners here are seers, and being confounded the same with ashamed, this ingemination adds to the thing spoken, at least a fuller verification of it.</ns0:note>: yea, they shall all cover their <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>upper lip.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> lips <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">So Lepers did, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 13.45. and men ashamed, and Mourners did thus, <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 24.17, 22. So these shall mourn and pine in their shame.</ns0:note>, for <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> no answer of God <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">God doth not answer them, rather because the Answer they had formerly given and pretended to be from God now appears not to have been from him, they should therefore by the sentence of the Law be stoned, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 13.10. & <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 13.3. so <ns0:hi>Elijah</ns0:hi> dealt with <ns0:hi>Baals</ns0:hi> Prophets, and 'tis like these false Prophets detected might fear the like from those they had deceived.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 ¶ But truly <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Notwithstanding this shame, and silence covering these false Prophets, yet saith <ns0:hi>Micah.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> I am full of power <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Courage, Vivacity, and Abi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lity becoming a Prophet of God.</ns0:note> by the spirit of the LORD <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Not from himself but from the Spirit of God given to him, and duly qualifying him to the faithful discharge of the Prophetic Office, and without fear, flatte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry, by-respects or self-seeking I have already and still do, and will declare the sins, duties and dangers of this People that they may repent, and be saved, or my God may be justified when he judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth, and this people may know the difference between a false and true Prophet.</ns0:note>, and of judgment <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">A Spirit of Judgment to discern aright times, and seasons, to discern right from wrong, truth from lies and pure worship of God from Idolatry, and what are the conse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quents of all these to a people who decline from the way of truth and purity, or adhere to it.</ns0:note>, and of might <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Resolution, undaunted in speaking Gods word to the greatest of men, as I have dared, I still do dare to tell the Heads of <ns0:hi>Jacob,</ns0:hi> and princes of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> what they do against God, and what God will do against them.</ns0:note>, to <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 58.1.</ns0:note> declare unto Jacob his transgression <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">With impartial Reproofs, with severe menaces from God to preach against <ns0:hi>Jacob</ns0:hi>'s Transgressions.</ns0:note>, and to Israel his sin <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The same repeated. All the Twelve Tribes have sinn'd and God will visit.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Hear this, I pray you, ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Whereas judgment should be their great delight, as it is of every good Magistrate; these had hearts that detested it, were weary of the directions of Gods Law in their Polity, and hated to be controuled by it.</ns0:note>, and pervert all equity <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Where you can, you wrest the Law to countenance your unequal proceedings, and wrong those you should right, and acquit those you should condemn. And there is many a wo denounced against such.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note place="bottom">This Verse is word for word the same in the former part of it, with the former part of the first <ns0:hi>verse</ns0:hi> of this Chapter; we refer thither for explication of it. The Prophet having assert<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed his Divine Call and avowed his Faithfulness in the Prophe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tick Office, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 8. he here gives us one more proof of it deal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing roundly with the Magistrates in both Kingdoms, <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah.</ns0:hi>

               <ns0:p n="10">10 They <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Heads, Princes, Judges and great-ones among them.</ns0:note> build up <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">En<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />large or beautifie, and fortifie</ns0:note> Zion <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The houses in <ns0:hi>Zion,</ns0:hi> or per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />haps may be meant the Temple and its buildings, and the Roy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />al Palace of the Kings of <ns0:hi>Iudah.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 22.27. Zeph. 3.1.</ns0:note> with <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>bloods.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> blood <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">With Wealth and Gifts which these Builders made themselves masters of by violence taking away the life of the Owners, or else fining and amercing them. By this course they wrested part of their Estates from them, by the other they seised all; they also for gain some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times acquitted the Guilty, and freed them in capital Cases, and so sold the blood of the Innocent.</ns0:note>, and Jerusalem with iniquity <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">By such Injustice <ns0:hi>Ieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem</ns0:hi> was brought to Ruin at last, though some particular Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons and Families did raise themselves, their Houses and Palaces to a present largeness and stateliness.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 1.23. Hos. 4.18. chap. 7.3.</ns0:note> The heads thereof judge for reward <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Whereas the Judges were Gods Deputies, to hear and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />termine Causes, as the merit of the Causes were found, with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out respect of persons; they should have been careful to give such judgment as God would give, for the judgment is the Lords, and he sits in the midst of the Judges. These corrupt Judges attended little to the Cause, but much to Rewards, and with them the greatest Bribe made the justest Cause, and he was most guilty who was poor and could not, or honest and would not, give the expected reward. This was most directly against the Law of God, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 23.8. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 16.19. and ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />presly cursed, yet 'twas the common course and practice with them.</ns0:note>, and the priests thereof teach for hire <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">These men should have impartially declared the Law of God to all, told them what was clean or unclean, what was prohibited, what permitted, what commanded; what was safe to them, being pleasing to God; and what dangerous to them, being offensive to their God; but these for hire would direct them how to please themselves, and though they broke the Law, not be guilty; to extort, yet not be guilty of Usury; to kill an Enemy, yet not be guilty of Murther, nor break the sixth Commandment; to be unnatural to Parents, yet not sin. Who paid them well should find them most excellently skill'd in the Casuistical Divinity the <ns0:hi>Iesuites</ns0:hi> at this day are Masters of.</ns0:note>, and the prophets thereof divine for money <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Which being extraordinary persons raised of God, and sent by him to deliver his Message impartially to all his people, to all Rankes of men among them without fear, flattery, preju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dice, or any by-respects. There were in this people at this day a sort of men called prophets, but were indeed meer Fortune<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tellers, as we call a vagabond sort of persons among us, and these made a Trade of Divining, and as if 'twere in their <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ower to frame future things to the mind and humour of men, for a good round sum of money they would sell prosperity to them; for they never told great good to come to any but such as gave a great reward, and little money with them never purchas'd the news of a great advantage, and who so had first the misery to be poor, that they could not buy, or else were wiser than to beleive these Impostors, these were sure to be told a sad story of troubles and afflictions. Many Disciples of <ns0:hi>Balaam,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.15. they loved the wages of unrighteousness.</ns0:note>: yet will they lean upon the LORD <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Whilest Magi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />strates, Priests and Prophets are thus abominably corrupt, yet they will presumptuously lean upon the Lord, and flatter them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves that he is present with them, that he owneth them as his peculiar people.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>saying.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> and say <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Yea, they boast so.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>Is</ns0:hi> not the LORD among us <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">As our God, our Shield, whereas he was among them, but provoked to be their Enemy, though they will not believe it.</ns0:note>? no evil can come upon us <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">So they do falsly conclude against all the word of God, and against all his true Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets admonitions. No evil of affliction such as War, Famine and Captivity can come upon them. Thus far these corrupt <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Therefore shall Zion <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">By this it appears, that this Sermon was preach'd to <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> and its Governours, Priests and Prophets who were thus wicked in <ns0:hi>A<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>az</ns0:hi> his time, and probably continued so in the beginning of <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi>'s time; <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> does put this out of all doubt, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 26.18. saying that <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> spake these words to all <ns0:hi>Iudah.</ns0:hi> As for the time, it was in all likelihood before the thirteenth year of <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> say some; I rather think 'twas in the very beginning of <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> and that this might awaken them of that Age to comply with <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> in the Reformation. <ns0:hi>Zi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> here is threatned as endangered, nay ruin'd by the sins of Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gistrates, Priests and Prophets, they thought that <ns0:hi>Zion</ns0:hi> should be their safety, hower'e they sin'd, God by his Prophet assures them the quite contrary, their sins should be the danger and destruction of <ns0:hi>Zion.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> for your sake <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Because your sins are so great and ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny, God would have spared <ns0:hi>Sodom</ns0:hi> for the sake of righteous men, these may be safety to a City; but God will not spare the wicked for any places sake, nor shall a Temple be more secu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity to a wicked people, than Heaven was to sinning Angels. Though these flagitious men cry'd out against <ns0:hi>Micah,</ns0:hi> and such like men, as a publick danger, Truth is, the Injustice, Idola<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />try, and Inhumanity of publick persons were the great danger.</ns0:note> be <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">

                  </ns0:note> plowed <ns0:hi>as</ns0:hi> a field <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Either by the Enemy, and Conquerour, thereby forbidding it to be plowed without his leave, or by such as remained after the body of the People were carried Captive.</ns0:note>, and Jerusalem <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">One of the goodliest Cities of the World, proud in its lofty, and beautiful buildings, the City of the great king.</ns0:note> shall become heaps <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Shall all lie in rubbish, its stately buildings shall be demolished and lie buried in their own ruines.</ns0:note>, and the mountain of the house <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Holy mountain, on which the Temple, one of the Wonders of the World, did stand, beautified with rarest Buildings.</ns0:note>
                  <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> as the high places of the forrest <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Shall lye so long waste, as to be run over with Wood as a Forrest, and be a Lodge of wild Beasts.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
